scope: read-only analysis; no Java or database mutations

findings.claim: Headless shared backend has 10 HTTP request workers.
DirectThreadingStrategy uses one ReentrantLock for wrapped reads and writes, so calls using that strategy are serialised. It does not imply all reads are serialised.
get_functions is built directly on HTTP worker and deliberately bypasses threadingStrategy.
get_functions creates a separate DecompInterface per decompilation, disposing it in finally. No shared decompiler cache/object on this path.
get_metadata, read_memory, get_xrefs_to and get_xrefs_from use request-local containers and directly query the selected program, without executeRead wrapping.
Source exposes ProgramRevision in get_functions; fields restriction prevents unwanted caller decompilation.

limits: Client barrier measures simultaneously outstanding requests, not a full CPU execution trace. Ghidra internals can lock fine-grained resources.
These tests prove three independent read clients for one existing B database, not all possible tools, every function, or arbitrary counts of clients.
Requests involving simultaneous mutation of the same database need coordination; worker clones are the parent agent planned solution.

The shared backend currently auto-discovers a UDS endpoint before launcher routing isolation is repaired; identities matched B in the before-fix run, but that does not certify intended project/backend selection in multi-instance scenarios.
No measured speedup ratio is claimed.
